text: The account of Mehwish Zafar, a student with a declared monthly income of PKR 25,000, exhibits classic money mule characteristics. Between April 2 and April 11, 2026, the account received 28 inbound IBFT transfers totaling approximately PKR 1.4 million from 24 distinct counterparties across multiple banks (Synthetic Bank A, B, and C). This volume is significantly disproportionate to the customer's declared income and occupation. The funds were rapidly swept out of the account via three large wallet transfers to QuickPay wallet ***0932 (PKR 278,000 on April 4; PKR 305,000 on April 6; PKR 266,000 on April 10) and three ATM withdrawals at the Blue Area branch in Islamabad (PKR 111,000 on April 5; PKR 231,000 on April 7; PKR 115,000 on April 11). The pattern of receiving numerous small-to-medium transfers from unrelated individuals and immediately moving the aggregate value to a third-party wallet or cash is indicative of layering activities associated with money laundering. The geographic discrepancy between the customer’s residence in Karachi and the ATM withdrawals in Islamabad further heightens the suspicion. No legitimate business or personal explanation for this activity has been provided.
